The public-repository privacy prohibition and the broader nonpublic-disclosure rule address related but not identical boundaries.
Private generation context is a specific class of nonpublic information; both disclosure restrictions remain independently selectable.
Ontology human/machine representation and independently maintained public specimen presentation impose different Tarium requirements.
Choosing the latest stable supported edition and fixing edition 2024 can diverge when a later edition is supported. Conditional, not a proven current contradiction.
Repository inspection gathers source state; verifying Git branch and history checks a distinct repository invariant.
Default branch policy and verification of the actual branch are related but independently enforceable.
Change containment and prohibiting invented substitute project clones both restrict unauthorized deviations.
Rust formatting and Clippy lint checks verify distinct dimensions of code quality.
Unit and integration tests exercise distinct levels of Rust behavior.
Regression verification and unit tests are complementary testing practices.
Quality gates are a specific strengthening of continuous CI validation workflows.
Configuring continuous checks and confirming the actual CI outcomes require separate verification.
Maintaining README content and auditing consistency across project documentation are distinct duties.
Accurate roadmap records support but do not replace progress reporting for currently touched work.
Publication review supports the privacy prohibition without making the prohibition dependent on a scanner passing.
Secrets-control practices support the broader nonpublic-disclosure rule, while remaining independently applicable.
A semantic version policy and matching references to the current version are distinct responsibilities.
An inaugural release must tag the verified owner-accepted commit, a narrower condition than general release readiness.
Smoke tests and verification of all essential MVP workflows provide different levels of coverage.
Testable MVP acceptance criteria specialize general acceptance review for an inaugural baseline.
Evidence-based status labels and verifiable completion reports constrain different reporting steps.
Visual bars accompanying percentages specialize reporting of touched roadmap items.
Reporting touched items and the overall project progress provide complementary granularity.
Announcing first completion and suppressing repeated routine 100-percent announcements are complementary timing requirements.
Displaying stable identity colors in README refines the general visual identity requirement.
Differential C-versus-Rust verification is one specific method of checking strict-port fidelity.
Upstream feature coverage inventories specialize evidence of replacement capability for strict-port MVP.
Deferring nonessential work during strict ports and excluding future enhancements from MVP gates express complementary scope limits.
Defining purpose and specifying testable MVP criteria are distinct MVP planning operations.
End-to-end workflow tests and testing in the real target environment cover different requirements.
Passing applicable automated CI gates specializes the standing CI quality-gate practice at MVP graduation.
Blocking purpose-defeating defects and rejecting proxy-only graduation indicators are distinct safeguards.
Refusing proxy-only MVP completion claims specializes general evidence-based status reporting.
Preserving a graduated MVP baseline and recording its accepted compatibility promises are distinct duties.
Reconciling README, roadmap and milestone state at MVP graduation specializes ongoing README maintenance.
Approving a stable inaugural version and releasing the accepted exact commit are separate gates.
Tagging a verified commit and checking the resulting public release are separate verification activities.
Post-MVP change management specializes general backwards compatibility checks using the accepted compatibility contract.
No unrelated work through MVP inauguration is a specific instance of general change-scope containment.

Privacy prohibition forbids exposure of private Taria material; authorized externalization requires making a separately reviewed public-safe subset and forbids transplanting private source history. The externalization obligation does not require disclosing protected material.

The prohibition on disclosing private Taria resources is the protected boundary; prepublication inspection is a preventive control for that boundary. Reviewing source and artifacts does not authorize exposing them.

Publicly reproducible core operation and the prohibition of hidden private cross-project dependencies support the same outcome at different integration boundaries. Neither demands a dependency the other forbids.

A separately authorized clean-subset externalization workflow and the prepublication review of all output surfaces are separate, compatible checkpoints. The former prepares releasable material; the latter verifies exposure risks before release.

Pre-enrollment verification after owner authorization and ongoing accuracy of project manifests and membership claims concern admission and truthful state maintenance respectively. Neither grants or implies enrollment authority.
